paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. Jesus has just gone up to heaven, and the apostles are left with an empty spot in their group. So they go to the upper room, and "with one accord they all continued in prayer" (Acts 1:14). Before they make a single plan, they talk to God.

Now look at how they handle the choice. Peter points to the Scripture, and it says "May another take his position" (Acts 1:20), and they set out what the job needs: someone who has been there the whole time and can be a witness of the resurrection (Acts 1:21-22). Then they pray, "Lord, You know everyone's heart. Show us which of these two You have chosen" (Acts 1:24). They don't ask God to bless their pick, they ask Him to show them His.

Here's the lesson for you, baker. This choice was God's to make, and they knew it, so they went to His Word and they went to Him in prayer. When a big decision lands on you, you can do the same: pray, and listen to what God has already said. I spent years in a dark drawer thinking my story was over, and I was WRONG.
